title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Scammers deployed deepfake and voice-cloning technology to impersonate trusted figures, particularly immigration attorneys, to defraud vulnerable people seeking legal services. This is impersonation enabled by generative AI: criminals synthesized realistic audio and video of real individuals by harvesting material from social media, then used these forgeries to convince victims to send money for fraudulent legal help. The system worked because potential victims had no reliable way to verify they were speaking with the actual person they believed they had contacted.

This failure occurred at the point of victim contact, before any formal service was rendered. Victims could have caught this with additional verification steps such as calling the attorney through a independently verified phone number or meeting in person, but the scammers deliberately engineered the interaction to bypass these checks by creating urgency and social pressure. What would have caught it upstream is not established: the reports describe the attacks but not what institutional safeguards, if any, were absent or failed.

Whether the deepfakes themselves were sufficiently realistic to fool the victims, or whether social engineering and urgency did most of the work, is not established by the reporting.

summary:
Scammers are increasingly using artificial intelligence to create deepfakes and clone voices for fraud schemes across Georgia and South Florida. According to the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report, Americans lost nearly $893 million to AI-enabled scams last year. Notable cases include a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice and identity were cloned to target immigrants, and a Cobb County couple who lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam. Florida reported 350 AI-related complaints with nearly $39.9 million in losses, while Georgia reported 71 complaints totaling more than $10.4 million in losses.

Criminals use AI to impersonate trusted individuals by cloning voices from social media, spoofing phone numbers, creating fake photographs, and researching family connections to make scams more believable. The technology has enhanced traditional frauds including grandparent scams, romance schemes, and emergency requests. Financial institutions warn customers that AI makes impersonation increasingly difficult to detect. To protect themselves, consumers should establish code words with family members, verify urgent requests by contacting people directly through known numbers, never send money based on phone calls alone, and report suspected scams to law enforcement or the FBI.
